liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Shakedown Street** (3 reviews): Reviewer wanted Shakedown and was pleased to get it as a second opener right after the first song; Reviewer notes Shakedown as an East Coast breakout, but finds the jam thin given the recording [22][24][27]
- **Let the Good Times Roll** (2 reviews): The band sounds in good vocal form on the opening Let the Good Times Roll; Brent sings sweetly without screaming on the opener, according to the reviewer [24][27]
- **Let it Grow** (2 reviews): Reviewer calls this Let it Grow outstanding and one of their favorite versions; Reviewer singles out Let it Grow as especially hot within the first set [18][21]
- **To Lay Me Down** (1 review): Reviewer had seen this song at Hampton months earlier; this was the only other time they caught it live [22]
- **It's All Over Now** (1 review): Reviewer always welcomed It's All Over Now, preferring it to a Dylan cover [22]
- **Bertha** (1 review): Reviewer says Bertha had lyric trouble, though the rest of the show is strong [20]
- **Black Muddy River** (1 review): Reviewer rates this Black Muddy River as good as the band ever played it [20]

## Setlist highlights

- **Hey Jude refrain**: rare: 10 archived performances [30]

## The recordings

- **gd88-09-08.sbd.donaldson.1561.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 20 songs; 138 min; rated 3.36/5 by 14 [1]. Said about its sound: Sound is great but track splits are messy; several seconds of the Wheel intro are missing, likely from the master cassette; First-set sound is low, dull and plodding, lacking a sharp driving punch, which makes reviewing tedious; Sound is weak at the start of the first set, though another reviewer overstated how bad it is [20][24][25][26]
- **gd1988-09-08.142147.OTS.Schoeps.PCM.Mattes.Miller.Noel.t-flac1644**: source not stated; 19 songs; 152 min [2]
- **gd1988-09-08.136887.mtx.tobin.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 19 songs; 141 min; rated 3.5/5 by 2 [4]
- **gd1988-09-08.148085.sbd.ultramatrix.miller.pc.flac24**: soundboard; 19 songs; 143 min [6]

## Around the show

- Reviewer says city allowed camping in FDR Park, across Broad St from the Spectrum; the park scene beat the shows [18]
- On the off night of the four-night run, reviewer saw Tangerine Dream at the Tower Theater [18]
- Reviewer camped in the park across the street, and it didn't rain during the whole run [21]
- Reviewer's friends from Landover dropped away; they travelled alone to the last two Philly shows, then went on to NYC [25]
- First set is hotter than the solid second set, which doesn't quite match its level [21]
- Reviewer thinks there are many better shows from 1988 [26]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd88-09-08.sbd.donaldson.1561.sbeok.shnf**: source: SBD>Metal Cassette Master>DAT [1]. Also: Soundboard to metal cassette master to DAT; Tascam DA20 and HHb850 to CDR by Tom Donaldson and others; CDR was extracted with EAC and converted to shn files by John A., from the Uncirculated '88 SBD tree [1]
- **gd1988-09-08.142147.OTS.Schoeps.PCM.Mattes.Miller.Noel.t-flac1644**: taped by Ted Mattes and Don Crandall & Chris Huron; transferred by Charlie Miller and Joe Noel; source: Don Crandall & Chris Huron Recording (OTS): Schoeps CMC4/MK4 > PCM (Nakamichi DMP-100) (Sony ESX-HiFi/L-750 Beta tape); Charlie Miller [2]. Also: Audience recording from the first-row tapers section, left side, using Ted's rig, manned by Don and Chris; Taped with Schoeps microphones; Charlie coordinated and the masters were shared by Ted [2]
- **gd1988-09-08.136887.mtx.tobin.flac16**: transferred by Kevin Tobin; source: Matrix 2 Source Mix - SBD (shnid=1561) SBD>Metal Cassette Master>DAT; Tascam DA20>HHb850>CDR by Tom Donaldson et al; CDR> EAC> CDR> EAC> MKW Utility> .shn… [4]. Also: Matrix mixing a soundboard and an audience source, mixed by an archive.org user and converted to FLAC in 2016 [4]
- **gd1988-09-08.148085.sbd.ultramatrix.miller.pc.flac24**: taped by Don Pearson and Dan Healy; transferred by Charlie Miller; source: UltraMatrix SBD > Cassette Master (TDK SA-X90) [6]. Also: Patch source came from Don Crandall, Chris Huron and Ted Mattes; pitch correction applied to tracks 04 through 06 [6]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Kirsten Michel: [1988-09-09 The Spectrum, Philadelphia, PA, USA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1988-09-09-the-spectrum-philadelphia-pa-usa/) [31]

Matrix mixing a soundboard and an audience source, mixed by an archive.org user and converted to FLAC in 2016
Recorded by Don Pearson and Dan Healy; Charlie Miller handled transfers and mastering
Patch source came from Don Crandall, Chris Huron and Ted Mattes; pitch correction applied to tracks 04 through 06
